tier1.text: Each sartorius is a muscle that lets us sit cross-legged. It flexes, or bends, both the knee and the hip. It also abducts the thigh, moving it out to the side, and turns it outward. This long, thin muscle runs from the pelvic bone to the top of the tibia, or shin bone.

quotes.quote: the sartorius is a band-like muscle that extends from the anterior superior iliac spine to the medial side of the proximal tibia. This versatile muscle flexes the leg at the knee and flexes, abducts, and laterally rotates the leg at the hip. This muscle allows us to sit cross-legged.
